title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 8th District
area: Hudson and parts of Essex and Union counties, including Jersey City, Union City, and Elizabeth.

context.text: Incumbent Robert Menendez Jr. won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 68.8% of the vote against Mussab Ali. The Republican Party primary was canceled after no Republican candidates filed for this seat.
The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index rates the district D+15.

candidates.name: Robert Menendez Jr.

summary.text: Robert Menendez Jr. is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 and sworn in January 2023. An attorney raised in Union City, he previously served on the Hudson School Board of Trustees and as a commissioner of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and is Vice Chair of Policy for the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

background.text: Born in Englewood, New Jersey; according to his official biography, he was raised in Union City as the grandson of Cuban immigrants.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2008 and a J.D. from Rutgers University Law School in 2011.
Worked as an attorney, including at the law firm Lowenstein Sandler LLP, according to his official biography.
Served on the Hudson School Board of Trustees.
Served as a commissioner of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, where, according to his office, he chaired the Governance and Ethics Committee and sat on the Finance Committee.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and sworn in on January 3, 2023, representing most of Hudson County, the East and North Wards of Newark, and the City of Elizabeth.

In his second term serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and its Energy, Environment, and Communications and Technology subcommittees; earlier in the 118th Congress he served on the Homeland Security and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.
Serves as Vice Chair of Policy for the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and as a Regional Whip for the House Democratic Caucus, according to his official biography.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Communications and Technology, Environment, and Energy subcommittees.

During the 118th Congress (2023-2024), served on the Committee on Homeland Security, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit subcommittees), and the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, where he chaired the Subcommittee on Securities, Insurance, and Investment.

candidates.researchNotes: Limited additional record found beyond committee assignments; his official press-release feed was not accessible for this research.

candidates.name: Craig Honts

summary.text: Craig Honts is the Socialist Workers Party candidate for New Jersey's 8th Congressional District.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey response, or other public statements were found for Craig Honts beyond his Ballotpedia listing and party affiliation.

candidates.name: Da'Shone Hughey

summary.text: Da'Shone Hughey is the We The People Party candidate for New Jersey's 8th Congressional District. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is a technology executive, entrepreneur, educator, and author who founded CODEIT Institute of Technology, and he is running on workforce development, transit-linked housing, and domestic energy and manufacturing.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists his education as Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge College (graduate), and Nova Southeastern University's Shepard Broad College of Law, and his profession as CEO.

Describes himself as a systems builder, entrepreneur, technology executive, educator, and workforce-development strategist; says he founded CODEIT Institute of Technology and created AI City Robotics and Queriosity.
Says he studied at Hebrew University in Jerusalem, created operations in East Africa, and worked in Latin America.
Says he has been recognized by Marquis Who's Who in America and is the author of PhD Ready by 18.

candidates.researchNotes: Biographical details for Da'Shone Hughey come from his own Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no independent news profile was found.

candidates.name: Aristotle Eliopoulos

summary.text: Aristotle "Ari" Eliopoulos is an independent candidate for New Jersey's 8th Congressional District. He describes himself as an educator, union leader, and special needs advocate, the son of working-class immigrants. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is running on education reform, healthcare affordability, and independence from party establishments.

background.text: Describes himself as the son of working-class immigrants, raised to believe that hard work, education, community, and service are foundations of a strong society.
Works as a teacher and union leader; says his classroom experience shaped his focus on students, families, and educators.
Describes special needs advocacy as the policy issue he is most passionate about, citing his work as an educator with students with disabilities and their families.
Is running as an independent; says his campaign principle is "Results, Not Rhetoric."

priorities.text: Education reform that "puts students first," including strengthening public schools, expanding vocational and career education, and prioritizing special-education enforcement and resources.
Healthcare reform to lower prescription drug costs, increase price transparency, and expand mental-health services and access in underserved communities.
Lowering the cost of housing, healthcare, energy, and everyday essentials, and reducing regulations he says drive up prices.

positions.summary: Supports lowering prescription drug costs and expanding access to mental-health and preventive care, while also emphasizing competition among providers and insurers and reducing administrative bureaucracy.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website was located; positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
